newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end flat in the long end, up in short.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end flat in the long end, up in short.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended a shortened Christmas Eve trading session flat at the long end of the yield curve, but up slightly in the short end, dealers said.
They said trading interest was muted ahead of the Christmas and Boxing Day holidays on Wednesday and Thursday.
Trading will reopen on Friday for a recommended short day, the Toronto Bond Traders Association said.
The association recommended that trading on Friday ends at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.

In economic news, Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.3 percent in October after rising an upwardly revised 0.2 percent in September, Statistics Canada said. The government agency said the rise in GDP occurred despite of a 20-day strike in the auto sector.

"The strong 0.3 percent increase in GDP for the month occurred despite a long strike in the motor vehicle industry," Statistics Canada said in its report. "Excluding manufacturers of motor vehicles and parts, GDP advanced 0.6 percent."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond ended flat at a price of 111.50 for a yield of 7.035 percent.

Canada's two-year bond rose C$0.08 to 103.60 to yield 4.055 percent. In the money market, Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill yield ended the day down one basis point at 2.89 percent from Monday's close.
